'''Anashi-ni-imasu Hyōzu Shrine''' ({{nihongo|穴師坐兵主神社|あなしにますひょうずじんじゃ|qq=}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Sakurai, Nara|en|Sakurai, Nara|qid=Q127026|lt=Sakurai}}, Nara Prefecture, Japan. The shrine is listed among the {{ill|8=ja|9=Yamato Province の式内社一覧|List of Shikinaisha in Yamato Province|lt=Shikinaisha in Yamato Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/8=ja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and was formerly classified as a [[Ken-sha|prefectural shrine]] ({{nihongo|Ken-sha|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|qid=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Metropolitan_and_Prefectural_Shrines|qq=}}).
The shrine was originally composed of three separate shrines: {{nihongo|Anashi-ni-imasu Hyōzu Shrine|穴師坐兵主神社|qq=}}, a Myōjin Taisha, {{nihongo|Makimuku-ni-imasu Wakumusubi Shrine|巻向坐若御魂神社|qq=}}, a Shikinaisha Taisha, and {{nihongo|Anashi-no-Ōhyozu Shrine|穴師大兵主神社|qq=}}, a Shikinaisha Shōsha. These were combined during the {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}} into the current site, which was originally the location of Anashi-no-Ōhyozu Shrine.
== History ==
The origins of the shrine are unclear. According to one tradition, the original Anashi-ni-imasu Hyōzu Shrine was established by {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} in the 2nd year of the reign of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin}} to enshrine the guardian deity of the emperor’s meals. Another tradition attributes its founding to {{ill|Emperor Keikō|en|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723|lt=Emperor Keikō}}, who enshrined [[Ōkuninushi]] as Hyozu-no-Kami. Its original location, identified as {{nihongo|Yuzuki-dake|弓月岳|qq=}}, has been variously associated with Ryūōzan, Anashiyama, and Makimukuyama mountains.
The shrine's primary deity, Hyozu-no-Kami, is currently enshrined in the central hall and is represented by a sacred mirror. The shrine identifies Hyozu-no-Kami with Miketsu-no-Kami, though other interpretations link the deity to [[Ame-no-Uzume]], [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]], Tenfukino-Mikoto, {{ill|Takeminakata|ja|建御名方命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qid=Q9150391}}, or {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}}.
The former {{nihongo|Makimuku-ni-imasu Wakumusubi Shrine|巻向坐若御魂神社|qq=}} was located in Makimukuyama and enshrined Wakumusubi-no-Kami, now interpreted as Kushinada-hime and represented by magatama beads and bells. Some theories associate Wakumusubi-no-Kami with {{ill|Wakumusubi|ja|和久産巣日神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakumusubi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ワクムスビ}}.
The oldest records of these shrines appear in the [[Shōsōin]] documents, which mention rituals performed in 730 CE. In 859 CE, Anashi-ni-imasu Hyōzu Shrine was granted the Rank of {{ill|Senior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|正五位上|1=Senior Fifth Rank|lt=Senior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Fifth Rank|qq=}}, while Makimuku-ni-imasu Wakumusubi Shrine received {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|従五位上|1=Junior Fifth Rank|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fifth Rank|qq=}}.
The origins of Anashi-no-Ōhyozu Shrine are unknown. Its deity, Ōhyozu-no-Kami, is enshrined in the left hall and is represented by a sacred sword. The deity has been identified as {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Hiboko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノヒボコ}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}}, or Susanoo.
During the {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}}, the shrine’s main structures were destroyed during the {{ill|Ōnin War|en|Ōnin War|qid=Q385676|lt=Ōnin War}}. The remaining shrines were consolidated at the location of Anashi-no-Ōhyozu Shrine. In 1873, the shrine was designated a {{nihongo|gōsha|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|qq=}}, and in 1928, it was elevated to the Rank of prefectural shrine.
== Subordinate Shrines ==
A subsidiary shrine on the premises honors {{nihongo|[[Nomi no Sukune]]|野見宿禰|qq=}}, revered as the ancestor of sumo wrestling.
== Access ==
* A 30-minute walk east from {{ill|Makimuku Station|en|Makimuku Station|qid=Q4980794|lt=Makimuku Station}} on the {{ill|West Japan Railway Company|en|West Japan Railway Company|qid=Q502125|lt=West Japan Railway Company}} {{nihongo|Sakurai Line|桜井線|qq=}}.
